600: from ἀπό and καθίστημι; to reconstitute (in health, home or organization):--restore (again).
601: from ἀπό and καλύπτω; to take off the cover, i.e. disclose:--reveal.
602: from ἀποκαλύπτω; disclosure:--appearing, coming, lighten, manifestation, be revealed, revelation.
603: from a comparative of ἀπό and a compound of (the head) and δοκέω (in the sense of watching); intense anticipation:--earnest expectation.
604: from ἀπό and καταλλάσσω; to reconcile fully:--reconcile.
606: from ἀπό and κεῖμαι; to be reserved; figuratively, to await:--be appointed, (be) laid up.
607: from ἀπό and κεφαλή; to decapitate:--behead.
608: from ἀπό and κλείω; to close fully:--shut up.
609: from ἀπό and κόπτω; to amputate; reflexively (by irony) to mutilate (the privy parts):--cut off. Compare κατατομή.
610: from ἀποκρίνομαι (in its original sense of judging); a judicial decision:--sentence.
611: from ἀπό and ; to conclude for oneself, i.e. (by implication) to respond; by Hebraism (compare עָנָה) to begin to speak (where an address is expected):--answer.
613: from ἀπό and κρύπτω; to conceal away (i.e. fully); figuratively, to keep secret:--hide.
614: from ἀποκρύπτω; secret; by implication, treasured:--hid, kept secret.
615: from ἀπό and (to slay); to kill outright; figuratively, to destroy:--put to death, kill, slay.
616: from ἀπό and the base of κῦμα; to breed forth, i.e. (by transference) to generate (figuratively):--beget, produce.
617: from ἀπό and κυλιόω; to roll away:--roll away (back).
618: from ἀπό and λαμβάνω; to receive (specially, in full, or as a host); also to take aside:--receive, take.
619: from a comparative of ἀπό and (to enjoy); full enjoyment:--enjoy(-ment).
620: from ἀπό and λείπω; to leave behind (passively, remain); by implication, to forsake:--leave, remain.
621: from ἀπό and (to "lick"); to lick clean:--lick.
622: from ἀπό and the base of ὄλεθρος; to destroy fully (reflexively, to perish, or lose), literally or figuratively:--destroy, die, lose, mar, perish.
623: active participle of ἀπόλλυμι; a destroyer (i.e. Satan):--Apollyon.
624: from the pagan deity (i.e. the sun; from ἀπόλλυμι); Apollonia, a place in Macedonia:--Apollonia.
625: probably from the same as Ἀπολλωνία; Apollos, an Israelite:--Apollos.
626: middle voice from a compound of ἀπό and λόγος; to give an account (legal plea) of oneself, i.e. exculpate (self):--answer (for self), make defence, excuse (self), speak for self.
627: from the same as ἀπολογέομαι; a plea ("apology"):--answer (for self), clearing of self, defence.
628: from ἀπό and λούω; to wash fully, i.e. (figuratively) have remitted (reflexively):--wash (away).
629: from a compound of ἀπό and λύτρον; (the act) ransom in full, i.e. (figuratively) riddance, or (specially) Christian salvation:--deliverance, redemption.
630: from ἀπό and λύω; to free fully, i.e. (literally) relieve, release, dismiss (reflexively, depart), or (figuratively) let die, pardon or (specially) divorce:--(let) depart, dismiss, divorce, forgive, let go, loose, put (send) away, release, set at liberty.
631: middle voice from ἀπό and (to squeeze, knead, smear); to scrape away:--wipe off.
632: from ἀπό and the base of νόμος; to apportion, i.e. bestow:--give.
633: from ἀπό and νίπτω; to wash off (reflexively, one's own hands symbolically):--wash.
634: from ἀπό and πίπτω; to fall off:--fall.
635: from ἀπό and πλανάω; to lead astray (figuratively); passively, to stray (from truth):--err, seduce.
636: from ἀπό and πλέω; to set sail:--sail away.
637: from ἀπό and πλύνω; to rinse off:--wash.
638: from ἀπό and πνίγω; to stifle (by drowning or overgrowth):--choke.
639: from a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and the base of πορεύομαι; to have no way out, i.e. be at a loss (mentally):-- (stand in) doubt, be perplexed.
640: from the same as ἀπορέω; a (state of) quandary:--perplexity.
641: from ἀπό and ῥίπτω; to hurl off, i.e. precipitate (oneself):--cast.
642: from ἀπό and a derivative of ὀρφανός; to bereave wholly, i.e. (figuratively) separate (from intercourse):--take.
643: from ἀπό and a derivative of σκεῦος; to pack up (one's) baggage:--take up… carriages.
644: from a compound of ἀπό and a derivative of σκιά; a shading off, i.e. obscuration:--shadow.
645: from ἀπό and σπάω; to drag forth, i.e. (literally) unsheathe (a sword), or relatively (with a degree of force implied) retire (personally or factiously):--(with-)draw (away), after we were gotten from.
646: feminine of the same as ἀποστάσιον; defection from truth (properly, the state) ("apostasy"):--falling away, forsake.
647: neuter of a (presumed) adjective from a derivative of ἀφίστημι; properly, something separative, i.e. (specially) divorce:--(writing of) divorcement.
648: from ἀπό and a derivative of στέγη; to unroof:--uncover.
649: from ἀπό and στέλλω; set apart, i.e. (by implication) to send out (properly, on a mission) literally or figuratively:--put in, send (away, forth, out), set (at liberty).
650: from ἀπό and (to deprive); to despoil:--defraud, destitute, kept back by fraud.
652: from ἀποστέλλω; a delegate; specially, an ambassador of the Gospel; officially a commissioner of Christ ("apostle") (with miraculous powers):--apostle, messenger, he that is sent.
653: from ἀπό and a (presumed) derivative of στόμα; to speak off-hand (properly, dictate), i.e. to catechize (in an invidious manner):--provoke to speak.
654: from ἀπό and στρέφω; to turn away or back (literally or figuratively):--bring again, pervert, turn away (from).
655: from ἀπό and the base of στυγνητός; to detest utterly:--abhor.
656: from ἀπό and συναγωγή; excommunicated:--(put) out of the synagogue(-s).
657: middle voice from ἀπό and τάσσω; literally, to say adieu (by departing or dismissing); figuratively, to renounce:--bid farewell, forsake, take leave, send away.
658: from ἀπό and τελέω; to complete entirely, i.e. consummate:--finish.
659: from ἀπό and τίθημι; to put away (literally or figuratively):--cast off, lay apart (aside, down), put away (off).
660: from ἀπό and (to jostle); to brush off:--shake off.
661: from ἀπό and τίνω; to pay in full:--repay.
662: from ἀπό and τολμάω; to venture plainly:--be very bold.
663: from the base of ἀποτόμως; (figuratively) decisiveness, i.e. rigor:--severity.
664: adverb from a derivative of a comparative of ἀπό and (to cut); abruptly, i.e. peremptorily:--sharply(-ness).
665: from ἀπό and the base of τροπή; to deflect, i.e. (reflexively) avoid:--turn away.
666: from the participle of ἄπειμι; a being away:--absence.
667: from ἀπό and φέρω; to bear off (literally or relatively):--bring, carry (away).
668: from ἀπό and φεύγω; (figuratively) to escape:--escape.
669: from ἀπό and φθέγγομαι; to enunciate plainly, i.e. declare:--say, speak forth, utterance.
670: from ἀπό and the middle voice of φορτίζω; to unload:--unlade.
671: from a compound of ἀπό and χράομαι; the act of using up, i.e. consumption:--using.
672: from ἀπό and χωρέω; to go away:--depart.
673: from ἀπό and χωρίζω; to rend apart; reflexively, to separate:--depart (asunder).
674: from ἀπό and ψύχω; to breathe out, i.e. faint:--hearts failing.
675: of Latin origin; (in the genitive, i.e. possessive case) of Appius, the name of a Roman:--Appii.
676: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a comparative of πρός and (to go); inaccessible:--which no man can approach.
677: from Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of προσκόπτω; actively, inoffensive, i.e. not leading into sin; passively, faultless, i.e. not led into sin:--none (void of, without) offence.
678: adverb from a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of a presumed compound of πρόσωπον and λαμβάνω (compare προσωπολήπτης); in a way not accepting the person, i.e. impartially:--without respect of persons.
679: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of πταίω; not stumbling, i.e. (figuratively) without sin:--from falling.
680: reflexive of ἅπτω; properly, to attach oneself to, i.e. to touch (in many implied relations):--touch.
681: a primary verb; properly, to fasten to, i.e. (specially) to set on fire:--kindle, light.
682: probably of foreign origin; Apphia, a woman of Collosæ:--Apphia.
683: from ἀπό and the middle voice of or (to shove); to push off, figuratively, to reject:--cast away, put away (from), thrust away (from).
684: from a presumed derivative of ἀπόλλυμι; ruin or loss (physical, spiritual or eternal):--damnable(-nation), destruction, die, perdition, X perish, pernicious ways, waste.
685: probably from αἴρω; properly, prayer (as lifted to Heaven), i.e. (by implication) imprecation:--curse.
686: probably from αἴρω (through the idea of drawing a conclusion); a particle denoting an inference more or less decisive (as follows):--haply, (what) manner (of man), no doubt, perhaps, so be, then, therefore, truly, wherefore. Often used in connection with other particles, especially γέ or οὖν (after) or εἰ (before). Compare also ἆρα.
687: a form of ἄρα, denoting an interrogation to which a negative answer is presumed:--therefore.
688: of Hebrew origin (עֲרָב); Arabia, a region of Asia:--Arabia.
689: of Hebrew origin (רָם); Aram (i.e. Ram), an Israelite:--Aram.
690: from Ἀραβία; an Arab or native of Arabia:--Arabian.
691: from ἀργός; to be idle, i.e. (figuratively) to delay:--linger.
692: from Α (as a negative particle) and ἔργον; inactive, i.e. unemployed; (by implication) lazy, useless:--barren, idle, slow.
693: from ἄργυρος; made of silver:--(of) silver.
694: neuter of a presumed derivative of ἄργυρος; silvery, i.e. (by implication) cash; specially, a silverling (i.e. drachma or shekel):--money, (piece of) silver (piece).
695: from ἄργυρος and κόπτω; a beater (i.e. worker) of silver:--silversmith.
696: from (shining); silver (the metal, in the articles or coin):--silver.
697: from (the name of the Greek deity of war) and a derivative of πήγνυμι; rock of Ares, a place in Athens:--Areopagus, Mars' Hill.
698: from Ἄρειος Πάγος; an Areopagite or member of the court held on Mars' Hill:--Areopagite.
699: from a derivative of ἀρέσκω; complaisance:--pleasing.
